Subject: RFI: Rate Slicing, Overage Governance & Billing Examples

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking Meridian Tech's RFP. A couple of clarifying asks from procurement before we schedule pricing reviews:

1) Can you provide a worked example that shows unit token pricing across three phases (pilot -> ramp -> steady-state) including any onboarding credits? We need clear assumptions (model family, average prompt/response length, % streaming) so we can compare apples-to-apples.

2) For committed arrangements, how do you treat overages that are short duration bursts versus sustained sustained exceedances? Do you invoice immediately at an overage rate, or aggregate into a monthly true-up? Any smoothing/forgiveness bands?

3) We have multiple business units that would like pooled billing but independent sub-account limits. Does Redwood support account-level rate-slicing (e.g., shared commit with per-subaccount throttles and allocation rules)? How are credits/true-ups apportioned?

4) Please include your standard SLA credit treatment when overages push customers into our backup model variants (e.g., quantized LLMs) — specifically how credits are applied if Redwood fails to meet latency SLO and we failover to a higher-cost fallback.

If you can attach a short appendix with line-item examples and a sample invoice, that would be ideal. Happy to set a 30-minute follow-up after we digest the appendix. Procurement would like this by end of week.

Regards,
Oliver
Director, Cloud Procurement
Meridian Tech

Hi Oliver,

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks. I've attached a compact appendix (Redwood-RateSlicing-AppendixA.xlsx) that includes worked line items and a sample monthly invoice. High-level answers below; Marissa and Karthik are cc'd to validate commercial terms and provide numeric scenarios.

1) Worked pricing examples: appendix contains three scenarios (Pilot: 100M tokens; Ramp: 450M; Steady: 1B). We assume the following baseline for all examples: base LLM family = redwood-v2-medium, average request+response = 500 tokens, 20% streaming, 80% generation. Unit list price used = $0.0012/token (on-demand).

2) Overage treatment: we support two governance modes — Immediate Overage Billing (IOB) and Monthly True-up (MTU):
  - IOB: Overage charged at 1.25x list unit for the billing period in which it occurs; useful for short, infrequent bursts to avoid deferred accounting complexity.
  - MTU: Overage aggregated and billed at month-end at a discounted overage multiplier (typically 1.10x of committed unit price), with smoothing bands where a single-month exceedance within a 3-month window can be absorbed into the next month's allocation up to a configurable cap.

3) Pooled billing + allocation: Redwood supports a single invoice and pooled commit. Allocation rules we offer: pro-rata by committed capacity, priority allocation (business-unit weight), and hard caps per sub-account. True-up distribution options include proportional charge-back or prioritized bucket offset; appendix shows worked examples.

4) SLA credits & fallback: if Redwood's routing fails and the request is served by a fallback variant that materially degrades latency SLOs, we offer SLA credits based on the percentage of requests impacted and time out-of-SLO. Credits are applied as dollar offsets on the next invoice and are netted after any overage; see Appendix tab 'SLA Credits' for the formula.

I'll schedule a 30min slot after you confirm availability — proposed times today 3–5pm PT or tomorrow 9–11am PT.

Best,

Marissa / Karthik,

Forwarding Meridian's procurement asks (below). They want concrete numbers in the appendix; Oliver expects us to show pilot -> ramp -> steady comparisons and a sample invoice. Quick ask: can you validate the proposed numbers and give a recommended commercial stance?

My initial proposal (for the appendix):
- Pilot (100M tokens): flat fixed fee $15,000 (includes onboarding, 30-day trial model tuning); effective unit = $0.00015/token.
- Ramp (450M tokens / month): 6-month commit at $0.0009/token; overage MTU multiplier = 1.10x committed unit; smoothing band: first 10% of month-over-month delta absorbed for free.
- Steady-state (1B tokens / month): annual commit; base unit = $0.0008/token; tiers: >1.5B add'l tokens at $0.00072/token (10% tiered discount); overage IOB rate for short bursts 1.25x list ($0.0012) if immediate billing chosen.

SLA/fallback: offer credit ladder (5% invoice credit for 1st qualifying incident, 10% subsequent within quarter) and a 2% onboarding credit applied on the first invoice after contract signature.

Questions for you:
- Are these rates competitive / margin-safe?
- Do we want to attach an optional 12-week pilot conversion credit (2% of first-year committed spend) if they convert to annual within 90 days?

Quick replies appreciated — I'm planning to send a polished response back to Meri by 2pm PT.

Thanks,
Sofia

Hi Oliver / Priya,

Thanks for the patience — attached is a consolidated appendix that incorporates the worked examples and a sample invoice. Key commercial summary below (pulled from Appendix tab 'Summary'):

- Pilot: $15,000 fixed fee for up to 100M tokens, includes onboarding & pilot support (effective $0.00015/token).
- Ramp (6-month): 450M tokens/month commit at $0.0009/token. Monthly true-up (MTU) by default; overage multiplier 1.10x committed unit. Smoothing: first 10% mm delta absorbed once per quarter.
- Steady (annual): 1B tokens/month commit at $0.0008/token with tiered discounts (10% at >1.5B). Optional burst cushion: pre-purchased burst bucket (100M tokens) at $0.00085/token that expires monthly, available for guaranteed low-latency workloads.

Invoice cadence & true-up: monthly invoices with line-item for committed usage, overage (if MTU chosen), and any SLA credits applied as negative line items. Sample invoice included in Appendix shows how pooled billing and per-subaccount allocation appear (we support both proportional and priority allocation methods).

SLA credits & failover: Credits applied as invoice offsets; formula in Appendix: credit = (impacted_requests / total_requests) * SLA_band_credit_rate. If failover to a higher-cost fallback variant occurs due to routing/capacity, we commit to bearing the incremental compute cost above the committed unit price for incidents covered by our routing error (subject to verification).

Flex credits: Redwood can extend a 2% first-year conversion credit if Meridian signs an annual commit within 90 days of pilot completion.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether Meridian prefers IOB or MTU for overage handling.
- If MTU, confirm desired allocation rule (pro-rata vs priority).

If useful, we can produce a one-page 'billing playbook' showing a 1B-token worked example converting from on-demand to committed pricing (I can run that with finance and attach by EOD).
